subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Chris Nguyen <chris.nguyen@finbot.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Chris —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call so we have shared alignment and clear next steps. If I missed anything, please reply with edits.

Pain points you confirmed:
- Unit economics: current per-inference cost is squeezing margins; target is ~60% reduction to support S&M growth.
- Peak latency sensitivity: p95 target for user-facing flows <= 300ms.
- Traffic profile: lots of short, repetitive prompts with occasional long-context requests (~1,200 tokens).
- Operational constraints: HIPAA-esque compliance posture and preference for a managed private deployment or dedicated pool.

Current stack (what you told us):
- Frontend calls -> service layer -> OpenAI (gpt-4o) via API today.
- Peak ~120 reqs/sec, monthly ~10M tokens.
- Some local caching at app layer but no token-level KV cache today.

Success criteria for pilot/POC:
1) Cost: demonstrate >50% reduction in per-inference $/user compared to current spend (model + infra).
2) Latency: p95 <= 300ms for the most common short flows.
3) Quality: no material drop in user satisfaction (>95% of current quality judged by your eval set).

Technical openness you indicated:
- Happy to consider quantized model variants if quality stays within your threshold.
- Interested in automatic batching + prefix/KV caching to reduce tokens and cost.

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
- I will share a Mutual Action Plan (attached) and a short list of items we need for a scoped cost model (sample traffic, request/response sizes, current token counts). Attachment: 20260322-FinBot-MAP.pdf.
- You to share a small representative traffic sample (anonymized) and any existing perf budgets. Link: https://drive.google.com/finbot-sample-traffic
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your engineering lead + our solutions engineer to validate batching/caching approach (proposed window below).

Proposed windows for a 60-minute technical session:
- Wed 3/24 10:00–11:00 PT
- Thu 3/25 13:00–14:00 PT

Attachments: 20260322-FinBot-MAP.pdf, SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx (we can redact fields for now).

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Chris Nguyen <chris.nguyen@finbot.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jill Carter <jill.carter@finbot.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Thanks for the clear write-up, Marissa — this is exactly what I was hoping for. A few clarifications / additions from our side: 

- Current stack: we call OpenAI (gpt-4o) via gateway; model latency averages ~220ms but p95 spikes to ~700ms during peak.
- Typical request size: median 300 tokens, mean ~1,200 tokens because of occasional long contexts.
- Monthly volume: ~10M tokens, peak ~120 rps.
- Caching interest: high — especially prefix caching for repetitive prompts in our customer support assistant.
- Quantization: our ML lead is open to 8-bit/4-bit quantized models provided we run an A/B on quality; any drop beyond 3–5% in your eval metric is a non-starter.

I can share an anonymized traffic sample and our current perf budgets. I'll upload to the Drive link you included by EOD.

For the technical session, Thu 3/25 13:00–14:00 PT works for our eng lead (Jill). Please include your solutions engineer and someone from runtime/serving if possible.

Also: curious if you have a sense of how Redwood handles automatic batching for low-latency, high-QPS workloads (we need to avoid increased p95).

Thanks — Chris
Chris Nguyen
Head of Product, FinBot
chris.nguyen@finbot.com | (650) 555-0189

Perfect — thanks Chris. Quick replies inline below and a few action items for our teams.

On quantization: we can run 8-bit and 4-bit variants behind a canary A/B and surface quality regressions tied to your eval set; SE will propose thresholds and rollback rules.

On batching: Redwood supports adaptive batching that prioritizes latency-sensitive routes (we can pin the customer-facing assistant to a low-latency policy while batching lower-priority jobs). We'll have the runtime/serving engineer explain the tradeoffs in the technical deep-dive.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- FinBot: upload anonymized traffic sample + perf budgets to Drive (Chris / EOD 3/22) — DONE expected by EOD.
- Redwood: cost model + scoped MAP updated with pilot success criteria (Ben / 3/23).
- Redwood SE + Runtime: technical deep-dive and proposed canary plan (Marissa to schedule / 3/25).

I'll send calendar invites for Thu 3/25 13:00–14:00 PT and include Ben + our runtime SE.

Thanks again — excited to take this next step.
